reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E1 discusses long-range ordering and hierarchical structures in a different alloy (FeCoNiSiAl) and notes that excessive ordering degrades coercivity, which contradicts the premise that partial ordering increases it. E2 shows coercivity increase in FeCoNiMnCu films via RTA due to microstructural changes and strain, not partial ordering in bulk FeCoNi. E3 attributes coercivity increase to defects from HPT deformation, not annealing-induced ordering. None of the evidence demonstrates partial ordering in fcc FeCoNi enhancing coercivity
premises: Partial atomic ordering in fcc FeCoNi-based alloys can increase coercivity by enhancing domain wall pinning.
Short-range ordered regions can form in fcc high-entropy alloys without triggering a full phase change.
Annealing at ~550 °C is below the disorder–order transition for fcc FeCoNi and can induce partial ordering.
Increased magnetocrystalline anisotropy from ordering leads to higher coercivity.
Controlled annealing can raise coercivity above ~100 Oe while retaining high saturation magnetization.
